title: Tune an alarm for evidence, not one noisy point
description: Choose a telemetry trace, M-of-N rule, and all-missing policy. The newest configured periods update the modeled alarm state and operator consequence.

scenarios.label: Brief spike
scenarios.detail: One bad minute is surrounded by healthy periods.

scenarios.label: Clustered failures
scenarios.detail: Three bad periods appear inside the five-minute trace.

scenarios.label: Sustained failure
scenarios.detail: Every observed period breaches the threshold.

scenarios.label: Silent producer
scenarios.detail: No data arrives after the alarm was healthy.

missingTreatments.label: Missing
missingTreatments.operatorMeaning: The alarm admits that it cannot evaluate the signal.

missingTreatments.label: Not breaching
missingTreatments.detail: All missing periods are treated as healthy.
missingTreatments.operatorMeaning: Useful for a sparse metric that emits only when an event occurs.

missingTreatments.label: Breaching
missingTreatments.detail: All missing periods are treated as bad.
missingTreatments.operatorMeaning: Useful when silence from a continuous heartbeat is itself a failure.

missingTreatments.label: Ignore
missingTreatments.detail: All missing periods retain the previous alarm state.
missingTreatments.operatorMeaning: Prevents a state change, but can leave a stale state in place.

modelNote: This teaching model evaluates the newest N displayed periods. The CloudWatch sliding-window evaluator can retrieve older points from a wider evaluation range and fills missing values only when needed.
